annotations.text:
Default: the Stage look (glowing strings, glass gems, fret numbers on the floor) with Chart's dark palette and green accent, and Workbench's fonts.
The sliders button opens settings to mix look, colours and fonts from any preset.

A · Stage: glowing strings, glass gems, fret number on the floor under each approaching note. The most game-like and atmospheric.
Tradeoff: glow is the heaviest to render and the busiest to read at speed.

B · Chart: flat and high-contrast, fret number printed on every gem like tab. Easiest to read from a distance and the cheapest to render.
Tradeoff: the least stage energy.

C · Workbench: warm wood-and-brass board, muted string colours, serif lyrics. Calm and instrument-like.
Tradeoff: muted colours separate strings less sharply, and it is the furthest from what players are used to.

Same mechanics in all three: notes land on their string at the strike line; lit anchor zone with fret posts; fret numbers under the strings; chord boxes with names (dashed = repeated chord); sustain tails; H / P / slide / bend / harmonic / PM marks; phrase bar whose heights are phrase difficulty; lyrics top-left. Strings run low E on top, as when looking down at the guitar.
Song title, lyric lines and accuracy are sample placeholders.
